title: Generated RF readback semantic fixture; not bench evidence

outcome.cause: is_defalut is device-owned; we sent 1 and the device returned 0. That was the only semantic difference in the whole document.

before.provenance: Protocol-format fixture; no live operator record

after.provenance: OBSERVED AT THE BENCH, NOT CAPTURED VERBATIM. The raw post-write cmd-116 frame was not saved; only these properties were recorded. Capture the raw frame on the next write and fill in cmd116_payload_ascii.

findings.statement: The device clears is_defalut from 1 to 0 on any write to /factory/fpv_bb_freq.json. It is device-owned and must be excluded from readback comparison, with the transition recorded.
findings.consequence: Readback verification compares the document minus DEVICE_OWNED_KEYS. Band arrays remain the proof that a write applied.

findings.statement: The device re-serializes the file itself with no indentation: 2018 bytes in, 1088 bytes back.
findings.consequence: Payload length and MD5 can never match across a write and must never be compared across one. The cmd-115 MD5 stays an integrity check within a single read.

findings.statement: Key order survived the write intact: RFBoardType, bandC, is_defalut, bandA, bandB, bandD -- is_defalut still mid-document, where the device had it.
findings.consequence: ordered_equal stays. Readback comparison is not weakened to order-blind ==; the device gives no reason to.

still_unverified: The raw post-write cmd-116 payload bytes (see after.provenance).
The exact separator style the device emits (no indentation is established; whether it emits ', '/': ' or ','/':' is not).
The cmd-115 digest offset inside the 68-byte payload (docs/PROTOCOL_SPEC.md section 9.2).
